issues.legal_issue: A land acquisition is not procedurally vitiated when affected persons receive an opportunity to object and their objections are considered before the declaration.
material_facts: Notices inviting objections were issued to the affected farmers.
The respondent filed an objection, which was taken on record and considered before the declaration was published.
issues.conclusion: The claimed denial of an opportunity to object was not established, and the acquisition procedure was not vitiated on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 5-A and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, the objection process must precede the declaration; the record showed that an objection was filed and considered before the declaration. No earlier case was cited.

rule.if: acquisition_writ_appeal and objection_notice_given and affected_person_objected and objection_considered_before_declaration

predicates.acquisition_writ_appeal: The matter is an appeal from a judgment reviewing land acquisition proceedings.
predicates.objection_notice_given: The acquiring authority gave affected persons notice and an opportunity to raise objections.
predicates.affected_person_objected: An affected person filed an objection to the proposed acquisition.
predicates.objection_considered_before_declaration: The acquiring authority considered the objection before issuing the acquisition declaration.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a judgment reviewing an acquisition concerns a process in which notice was given, an affected person objected, and the objection was considered before the declaration, the procedure is not vitiated.

issues.legal_issue: Land vests in the State free from encumbrances after an award is made and possession is taken.
material_facts: An award was made for the acquired land.
Symbolic possession was taken on the date of the award.
The writ petition challenging the acquisition was filed afterward.
issues.conclusion: The land had vested in the State free from all encumbrances before the writ petition was filed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the making of the award and taking of possession as resulting in vesting of the land in the State free from encumbrances. No earlier case was cited.

predicates.acquisition_writ_appeal: The matter is an appeal from a judgment reviewing land acquisition proceedings.
predicates.award_made: The acquiring authority made an award for the land.
predicates.possession_taken: The acquiring authority took possession of the land.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a judgment reviewing an acquisition concerns land for which an award was made and possession was taken, the land is treated as vested free from encumbrances.

issues.legal_issue: Delay, construction of the public-purpose project elsewhere, failure to construct during pending litigation, and increased land prices do not by themselves invalidate an acquisition.
material_facts: The acquisition proceedings had reached the award and possession stage before the challenge was filed.
The challengers relied on the passage of time and argued that the acquisition's purpose no longer survived.
They also relied on the fact that quarters had been constructed elsewhere and that construction on the acquired land had not occurred while litigation was pending.
The challengers additionally relied on an increase in land prices.
issues.conclusion: Those circumstances did not establish an error of law in the acquisition notifications and did not warrant interference; the acquisition notifications were restored.
issues.legal_principle: A later lapse of time, the fact that the public purpose was served elsewhere, construction not proceeding because of pending litigation, or an increase in land prices does not by itself vitiate a notification under Section 4(1) or a declaration under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act. No earlier case was cited.

rule.if: acquisition_writ_appeal and (prolonged_delay or purpose_served_elsewhere or construction_delayed_by_litigation or land_prices_increased)

predicates.acquisition_writ_appeal: The matter is an appeal from a judgment reviewing land acquisition proceedings.
predicates.prolonged_delay: A challenger relies on the passage of time after the acquisition proceedings began.
predicates.purpose_served_elsewhere: The public purpose was served by carrying out the project at another location.
predicates.construction_delayed_by_litigation: Construction on the acquired land did not proceed while litigation was pending.
predicates.land_prices_increased: The value of the acquired land increased after the acquisition proceedings began.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a judgment reviewing an acquisition concerns a challenge based on delay, the purpose being served elsewhere, construction being delayed by litigation, or increased land prices, those circumstances do not invalidate the acquisition.
